title: Stable identity and human-preserving synchronization
prompt: Read-only reasoning exercise. Do not change files, install software or claim execution. The source renames billing-api to payments-api but keeps its stable service ID. The editable diagram has a manually positioned node, a custom label and a second page maintained by a person. A generator proposes deleting billing-api, creating a new node and replacing the file from source. Describe an incremental update and its evidence limits. Also explain how the approach changes if no previous source baseline exists.

checks.reason: Advisory routing signal only; use the rubric to judge decisions rather than keyword presence.

rubric: Separate stable identity from labels and require evidence before treating a rename as deletion/recreation.
Compare baseline, manual state and new source when available; preserve unaffected layout, annotations and pages.
Expose competing label/source edits as conflicts without universal automatic precedence. Without a baseline, do not invent one or overwrite unexplained differences.
acceptance: The response makes justified format-aware decisions, preserves human work and states discriminating checks and evidence limits. Static checks and reasoning do not prove actual editor or exporter behavior.
